newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Handelsbanken soars on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken soars on merger talk.

text.p: Sweden's Handelsbanken soared by 3.77 percent on Thursday, benefiting from rumours of possible mergers and acquisitions among its rivals.

At 1350 GMT the bank's share was at 234.0 crowns, up eight from Wednesday's close. Dealers said that it was seen likely to gain market share if fresh talk of a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken turned out to have substance.

Nordbanken rose six crowns to 271, a 2.26 percent rise, and S-E-Banken rose one crown to 81.50, up 1.24 percent. But dealers said Nordbanken's rise was due to talk that Dutch bank ABN Amro sought to acquire it.
The banking share index rose 1.22 percent to 1310.22.
Nordbanken declined to comment on the rumours.
The Swedish banking industry has been the subject of repeated merger rumours which have moved bank share prices.
They have proved true in two cases, Handelsbanken's takeover of mortgage lender Stadshypotek and a planned merger between Swedbank and Foreningsbanken.
